answer: Basalt Attestation Ledger. Each identity must publish a signed chain of micro-observations at unpredictable intervals; a random auditor spot-checks one, and missing it voids the chain. The cost: an attacker must staff parallel workers producing genuine continuous attention across every identity, since batch-generated replies fail the timing and context checks. Ember marks the audit window; a quill signs each observation, binding it to the worker's prior entry.
